reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's The Cat's Judgment (Book III); the crow's first-person telling at the birds' assembly is turned into third person with disclosure, linking to story 27.

The cat's holiness is a plainly stated trickster's disguise with no emblems of any real community; the Ganges, the sacrifice argument and the hell verses are omitted, and the content note says the story is not about any religion.
ಕೌಜುಗ is correct for partridge. Age band 12+: both innocent animals are killed and eaten in two calm sentences, never drawn, and the cat goes unpunished.
After review the rabbit refers to the cat in the neuter. No em dashes; the pause question comes before the outcome.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; seams measured at x=512 and y=512/1024; no text. One generation, no edits.
The crow, the partridge (plumper after panel 1), the hare and the grey tabby cat are consistent.
The cat wears no robe, beads or marks and carries no religious symbol; its holiness is only its pose. Nothing is caught, bitten or hurt; panel 6 shows only the empty burrow and the sad crow at dusk.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels, not in the app in dark mode.
